source_text: IV. Εἷς δὲ ὀνόματι Κόϊντος, Φρὺξ προσφάτως ἐληλυθὼς ἀπὸ τῆς Φρυγίας, ἰδὼν τὰ θηρία ἐδειλίασεν. Οὗτος δὲ ἦν ὁ παραβιασάμενος ἑαυτόν τε καί τινας προσελθεῖν ἑκόντας. Τοῦτον ὁ ἀνθύπατος πολλὰ ἐκλιπαρήσας ἔπεισεν ὀμόσαι καὶ ἐπιθῦσαι. Διὰ τοῦτο οὖν, ἀδελφοί, οὐκ ἐπαινοῦμεν τοὺς προσιόντας ἑαυτοῖς, ἐπειδὴ οὐχ οὕτως διδάσκει τὸ εὐαγγέλιον.
pass_a_gloss: But one man by name Quintus, a Phrygian lately come from Phrygia, upon seeing the wild beasts lost courage. And this man was the one who had forced both himself and certain others to step forward of their own will. This man the proconsul, after begging him at length, persuaded to swear and to offer sacrifice. Because of this, therefore, brothers, we do not commend those who come forward by themselves, since the gospel does not teach in this way.
pass_b_english: Now there was one man called Quintus, a Phrygian only lately arrived from Phrygia, who lost his nerve when he caught sight of the beasts. He was the very man who had compelled himself and certain others to step forward of their own accord and offer themselves.

The proconsul plied him with many appeals until he got him to take the oath and perform the sacrifice. For this reason, then, brothers, we praise none who come forward of themselves, for that is not what the gospel teaches.
